1.title: A phone line upgrade stops US flights
1.text: On Friday, all flights in the US stopped for more than four hours. A company was changing old copper wires to new fibre. A router sent too many messages and caused problems. Thousands of flights were late or cancelled. The US government says it was not a cyber-attack. It says the system needs a big fix.

2.title: Upgrade of old wires caused US flight stop
2.text:
A nationwide stop of flights in the US on Friday came from an upgrade of an old telecoms network, the transport secretary, Sean Duffy, said. A company called L3Harris was changing copper wires for fibre when it installed a router. The router started flooding other equipment with connection attempts.

Because of this, 17 of 22 air traffic control centres had problems with voice communication. The aviation agency needed 45 minutes to find the cause, because maintenance is written on paper. It then grounded all flights.

More than 8,500 flights were delayed and nearly 8,000 were cancelled on Friday, according to FlightAware. Duffy said the system needs a $50bn overhaul. A security official said there was no sign of a cyber-attack.

3.title: Old copper wiring upgrade behind longest US flight grounding since 9/11
3.text:
An upgrade to a decades-old telecoms network caused the longest nationwide grounding of flights in the US since the 11 September 2001 attacks, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Saturday. Part of a key communications system was being switched from copper wiring, so old it has been discontinued, to fibre.

The contractor L3Harris installed a router that began flooding others with 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, Duffy said. FAA administrator Bryan Bedford said 17 of 22 air route traffic control centres had instability in voice and ground communications. It took 45 minutes to find the problem because maintenance is logged on paper, he admitted, so the agency grounded all flights as a precaution.

Planes were on the ground for more than four hours. FlightAware counted more than 8,500 delayed and nearly 8,000 cancelled flights on Friday. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no sign of a cyber-attack.

Duffy said the system needs a complete overhaul that could cost $50bn. L3Harris said it is supporting the FAA investigation. An analyst, Miles O'Brien, described the system as a house about to be condemned.
